observed.source: Codex session rollout (CLI-recorded thread settings; not model-authored)

result.decision_rationale: The required unit gate passed on the pushed candidate. The relative state-root and enrollment-identity fixes are verified. Two correctness issues remain. A Windows path can reach the state reader after only part of the path was inspected, and a registry enumeration failure can produce a successful empty listing.

executed_verification: The CLI transcript records the guarded push of b66d17218f1de1da446b6918b0aa653840042024 followed by the pinned controller's unit gate on that commit. The receipt records exit 0 and an unchanged worktree. The log's SHA-256 matches the receipt.

The gate ran 202 tests with one supplemental live-model smoke test skipped. All 11 ListCommandTests passed, including the real Windows junction and symbolic-link cases, relative-root enrollment from three working directories, and mismatched state identity.
inspected: Verified the detached HEAD and mission digest. Read the full feature diff, changed-file list, operating guide, protocol, prior findings, developer dispositions, tool transcript, gate receipt and gate log.
Traced claim creation, registry discovery, path inspection, JSON reads, CLI dispatch and the behavior tests.
limitations: Runtime observations come from the controller-recorded Windows gate. The reviewer performed read-only inspection.

The link fixtures used local targets. The gate did not exercise a positively identified mapped network drive. The developer also disclosed a check-then-open race and lack of POSIX network-mount detection.
required_gaps: Verify that an incomplete component check cannot authorize a later state-file read under Windows path normalization.
Verify that failure to enumerate a populated registry produces a diagnostic and a nonzero exit.
source_inspection_only: The two remaining findings follow from the missing-component return in local_read_problem and the error-suppressing registry glob. Neither condition appears in the recorded tests.

findings.actual: On FileNotFoundError, local_read_problem returns None, the same result as a successful inspection. The caller then opens the original path. For ordinary Windows drive paths, Win32 can normalize away a missing component followed by `..`, leaving a reachable suffix whose junctions or links were never inspected.
findings.blocking_rationale: The uninspected suffix can redirect the read to network storage despite the command's local-only contract. This case requires no concurrent filesystem change.
findings.expected: The reader opens a state file only after checking the effective path through its final component. A failed inspection leaves the claim visible with a diagnostic.
findings.requested_correction: Represent a missing component separately from a successful inspection and stop before opening that path, or inspect and open the same safely normalized path. Preserve the empty result for an absent registry and the per-row diagnostic for missing state.
findings.requested_evidence: Extend the Windows fixture with a noncanonical state directory and a local junction in its effective path. Assert that the read tripwire stays clear, the affected row is unknown, and the healthy enrollment retains its fields.
findings.title: A missing path component ends link inspection before the state read
findings.trigger: A legacy or damaged claim contains an absolute Windows state directory with a missing intermediate component canceled by a later parent-directory segment.

findings.actual: Path.glob suppresses directory-scanning permission errors. When the directory metadata is readable but enumeration is denied, the loop receives no entries and the CLI prints `[]` with exit 0.
findings.blocking_rationale: An owner can receive a successful report of zero enrollments while the registry contains active claims.
findings.expected: An unreadable registry produces a nonzero exit and a diagnostic identifying the registry. A genuinely absent or readable empty registry prints `[]`.
findings.requested_correction: Enumerate the registry with an operation that exposes scan errors. Handle a missing registry as empty and report other enumeration failures through the CLI's refusal path.
findings.requested_evidence: Use a temporary populated registry whose directory permissions allow metadata inspection but deny enumeration. Assert a nonzero exit and a registry diagnostic. Retain the passing absent- and empty-registry cases.
findings.title: An unreadable registry is reported as empty
findings.trigger: The listing account can inspect the registry directory's attributes but lacks permission to list its contents.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: New claims record an absolute state_dir alongside the existing dir. The gate verified the actual enrollment fields from three directories with a decoy present, and retained the diagnostic for older relative-only claims.

The gate verified rejection of direct UNC paths, ordinary junction paths, linked claim and state files, and a linked registry. The missing-component branch still permits a read after the component walk ends early.

The reader checks enrollment identity before copying summary fields. The gate verified that mismatched and anonymous claims receive diagnostics, the healthy neighbor retains its fields, and a matching long-path claim returns its own PR.

summary.delivered_behavior: The documented list command returns sorted JSON with enrollment identity, status, phase, PR number and update time. Tests verified ordinary listing while the writer lock was held, an unchanged fixture tree, empty registries, and isolation of damaged claims and state files.
remaining_owner_review: Final acceptance of the corrected command and any merge or release decision.
summary.scope_reviewed: All five list-command requirements, the compatibility constraint, the pushed-candidate unit gate and all three pending findings.
